tagline: An AI research workbench for antimicrobial peptide design, where the application owns the research record and the model only ever receives a request.
summary: AMPilot is a live, hosted AI-assisted research workbench for antimicrobial peptide design, built around the argument that a conversation is an entry point but the research has to live in inspectable materials. Sources stay linked to their records, candidate sequences stay in files, and documents remain editable after the conversation moves on, across twelve implemented research stages grouped into five phases from framing a question to a bench handoff. The team wrote their own agent harness rather than using LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, DSPy or LiteLLM, specifically so the application rather than a framework owns the saved research state and the policy that turns it into model context, and so that a model proposal becomes an executable action only through a validated tool boundary. The sequence generator, TC-SRF, adapts the ProtFlow latent flow-matching pipeline with scientific-text conditioning via cross-attention and adaptive normalisation plus a constraint-aware decoder that refuses a residue unless some allowed suffix can still satisfy the stated length, charge and composition contract. Validation includes a 16-participant randomised AB/BA crossover user study, which is the most rigorous usability evidence any iGEM software team produced this year.

dry.frameworks: A Vue frontend rendering documents, files, questions and progress from server state, over a Python backend (Python 3.11, Node.js 22.12+) whose two named components are StudioRunner, which reads the workspace, runs the engine and reconciles delivery, and CompatibleEngine, which owns the inner model and tool loop and sends ordinary JSON over HTTP via httpx. Persistent state is SQLite with WAL, foreign-key checks and a busy timeout, holding tasks, sources, attachments, research items, questions, decisions and versioned documents, with transactions and version checks so a stale edit cannot silently overwrite a newer document. There are three deliberately separated entry points: five public scientific API routes that need no account, the authenticated hosted workbench (which locks the engine to the self-developed compatible path), and a local MCP bridge started with 'npm run mcp' that accepts a loopback backend and exposes a filtered read-only tool subset, with generation, evaluation, document writing and construct creation excluded by a mutating-tool filter. The team is explicit about what 'self-developed' does and does not mean: the dependency manifest has no agent framework, but ordinary libraries, external language models and scientific packages remain dependencies, and using an SDK would not inherently surrender control of message history; an optional Codex app-server adapter exists but delegates its inner runtime and is kept as a separate, non-conflated path. Licence Apache-2.0, with the TC-SRF-AMP generator MIT-licensed and carrying its own upstream attribution. Live at https://ampilotlab.com (Guest mode with checkpoints in the browser; API docs at /docs, OpenAPI at /openapi.json); source at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/xjtlu-software/ampilot, pinned at commit 31c2491 for the wiki.
dry.dataviz: The workbench presents a sequence workspace where a circular plasmid map and the base-level sequence stay connected to the original GenBank annotations, a public knowledge base with separate entry points into catalogues of sequences, MIC values, literature, drugs, clinical trials and patents, and a progress rail that makes unfinished stages visible. The rail's twelve stages are checked against saved outputs rather than against a conversational claim that a stage is complete, which is the key design idea. The measurement planner uses a typed claim rather than free text: a reading carries its quantity and endpoint, unit and subject, target organism, basis (predicted, observed or inferred), the model and the data it was fitted on, and the conditions and scope within which its interpretation applies, with compatible quantities and units checked at that boundary. Every screenshot on the wiki is captioned with its capture date (17 October 2026), the record shown, and an explicit statement that it illustrates the interface and not a biological outcome or a measured user benefit.
dry.datascience: Three layers of evidence, all dated and tied to commits. CI: on 2026-10-20 the team retrieved GitLab's job records and JUnit report for pipeline 776168 at commit 1ca9596, with all six jobs (lint, bundle, frontend, backend-rest, backend-science, backend-agent) passing: 2,622 backend tests passed with 43 skipped and 0 failures, plus 153 frontend tests. They then publish exactly what CI skipped and why (7 for a missing curated document index, 24 for an uninstalled clinical library, 2 for a missing research corpus, 2 for the unvendored HemoPI2 program, and so on), stating that the pipeline's fallback permits such skips so a green pipeline is not evidence every scientific model ran, and that a module skipped at collection can stand for more than one uncollected test. A separate fresh local full-suite run on a Mac mini at the same commit gave 2,677 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, and the team discloses that one installed regressor's digest differs from the public asset manifest, records both digests, and says the run tests the installed environment rather than certifying byte-identical assets. A local storage microbenchmark measured 400 reads and 400 writes across 8 workers on synthetic data (read 294.1 ops/s at P95 32.47 ms, write 2,895.6 ops/s at P95 4.86 ms, Python 3.11.16, SQLite 3.53.4, Darwin arm64, WAL with synchronous=FULL) and says plainly that this measures storage operations, not simultaneous users or model throughput. The TC-SRF checkpoint was inspected on 19 October 2026 under a restricted CPU load with a matching SHA-256: training step 10,000, best validation total loss 0.1246988252 at step 10,000, zero stale validation evaluations, with the team stating these are stored training state rather than a newly measured score and that they do not prove convergence, recover the loss trajectory or establish validation-set independence. The user study is the standout: 16 participants (8 bioinformatics postgraduates, 8 experimental researchers), each using both a conventional toolchain (PubMed plus web tools plus local scripts) and AMPilot, in a randomised AB/BA crossover with 8 per order, parallel tasks crossed with tools, and at least 48 hours between sessions. Tasks were salt-tolerant short cationic peptides for P. aeruginosa and protease-resistant short amphipathic peptides for MRSA. Results: completion 11/16 conventional vs 15/16 AMPilot; task time 142.5 +/- 28.6 vs 41.2 +/- 37.3 minutes with non-completions assigned the 180-minute cap, a paired reduction of 101.3 minutes (95% CI 81.4-121.2, SEM 9.35); operation and format errors 3.8 +/- 1.2 vs 0.4 +/- 0.5; System Usability Scale 58.2 +/- 9.4 vs 84.5 +/- 6.2. A completers-only sensitivity analysis is reported separately and labelled descriptive rather than paired because the subsets differ. The team states the study supports integration for these tasks and does not establish improved candidate activity, general effectiveness, or a population-wide usability ranking.
dry.software: The engineering argument is about who owns context, and it is the most interesting one in iGEM 2026. A long research task accumulates source passages, candidate evaluations, document versions and revised decisions; sending every repeated body is wasteful, but replacing them with a fluent model-written summary erases their identity and scope. AMPilot therefore constructs each request from explicit records with a preserved path back to omitted detail, under three stated rules (retention of identifiers, current verdicts and tool order; non-mutation, meaning a request is projected and the saved record is never overwritten; retrieval, meaning the place omitted evidence can be read again is always named). Concretely: the two most recent eligible search responses stay intact while older ones become source indexes only when the replacement is shorter, with a route back via read_source(source_id); the two most recent heavy analysis reads stay whole while older ones are truncated at 400 serialized characters per field without generating a new model-written summary, with a route back via read_research_item(item_id); and when the outer snapshot is rebuilt, revoked decisions move from confirmed_decisions into withdrawn_decisions so a retracted choice stops acting as a requirement while remaining in the audit record. Two loops with two responsibilities: an outer pass reads the workspace and builds the snapshot, while the inner provider loop projects a request-local copy of the message list, streams the response, validates and executes tool calls, matches results to tool-call IDs and appends receipts, with a 32-logical-response budget across a turn (and the honest note that transport retries and evidence-review calls fall outside that count). The tool registry supplies JSON Schema to the model and validates incoming arguments again on the server, refusing unknown tools, invalid arguments and mutations without an active task, and the wiki adds that a valid schema establishes a well-formed request, not a correct scientific conclusion. Delivery reconciliation is the mechanism that most directly addresses LLM failure: after the engine returns, StudioRunner checks promised work against saved outputs and outstanding questions, because 'a fluent closing message is not a delivery receipt', and if a summary fails evidence review after a report was already saved, a deterministic receipt links to the existing work instead of publishing the unchecked summary. Failure handling is designed rather than incidental: a stop records a cancelled task state, supersedes pending proposals, terminates the TC-SRF subprocess and kills it after a grace period, and rejects late publication by checking task status before any workspace write; a version conflict returns a conflict rather than overwriting, so an agent cannot silently restore figures the researcher removed; and an unresolved claim keeps the evidence and stores objections with the draft rather than treating them as approval. Five public API routes expose single functions without a chat thread: POST /api/v1/peptides/evaluate, POST /api/v1/peptides/assay, POST /api/v1/constructs/design (GenBank and SBOL out), GET /api/v1/corpus/search and POST /api/v1/measurements/plan, each row on the wiki carrying its own stated limit (the public corpus route is lexical and explicitly not the local BGE-M3 hybrid retrieval pipeline; the measurement route returns 503 when its bundle is unavailable). Reproducibility is staged honestly: a fresh checkout is described as a starting point rather than every runtime dependency, with predictor and explorer assets fetched through a manifest and SHA-256-checked, local artifacts rebuilt and content-checked, and optional neural services configured separately, with the note that fetched-file checksums and rebuilt-artifact content checks are different guarantees and that not all SQLite or serialized model files are byte-identical across platforms. Data lifecycle is recover-first: Trash stops active work and retains the research, permanent removal requires an exact-record confirmation plus a check that background work has stopped, file cleanup failures stay queued for retry, and the 30-day maintenance command is described as administrator-operated rather than an automatic timer, with the explicit statement that row deletion is not physical-media erasure and that the guide does not promise regulatory compliance. Deployment limits are named too: replicated recovery and a PostgreSQL migration remain work to validate before anyone describes this as distributed high availability. A smaller reusable amp-select package is published separately.
techniques: application-owned agent harness with bounded logical-response budget
non-destructive request projection with routes back to omitted evidence
delivery reconciliation of promised work against saved outputs
latent flow matching with text conditioning (cross-attention plus adaptive layer normalisation)
constraint-aware look-ahead decoding over length, charge, composition and fixed positions
typed measurement claims with unit and quantity compatibility checking
lexical and semantic (BGE-M3 hybrid) literature retrieval with provenance
randomised AB/BA crossover user study with paired analysis and 95% CIs

good.publicEngagement: Education is organised as three pathways (observe and explain; design and test; critique and deliberate) joined by adaptation and a shared foundation in synthetic biology and engineering thinking, reaching 6 learner groups, over 300 participants, 8 or more organisations and institutions, and 15 or more activities. The plan was built from expert advice before delivery rather than after: the team took the question of how to help people with very different backgrounds find their own way in to Dr Justin Fendos, trained at the Yale Teaching Center and founding director of the Dongseo Scientific Teaching Center in South Korea, across two visits, and shaped the plan around how he adapts materials to a syllabus and to a learner's stage. The stated aim was to teach the ideas behind synthetic biology even where they extend beyond AMPilot itself.
good.ihp: The guiding image is a ship built inside a glass bottle: it may have beautiful sails and never know whether it can withstand real wind. The team's framework insists software teams should not move from idea to implementation, but should ground the idea in social reality, narrow it to a real bottleneck, translate that into a scope, and only then develop along two parallel tracks of fitting real practice and learning to act responsibly. Stakeholders deliberately spanned clinical medicine, infection and antimicrobial resistance research, environmental science and One Health, and experimental AMP work, grouped by principal contribution and engaged at every stage rather than in one round of interviews. A respiratory physician with over ten years of clinical experience at Nanjing Brain Hospital, including severe respiratory infection and respiratory failure, and a documented case at a hospital in Wuhu, Anhui where a patient acquired a resistant infection, anchored the clinical reality. Environmental and One Health input then widened the frame from hospital treatment to the pathways by which antibiotics, resistant bacteria and resistance genes circulate, and the team records the resulting complication honestly: pollution sources, microbial communities and detection capacity vary, and no single indicator can fully describe the risk. The 16-participant crossover study is itself an integrated human practices output, run by the HP team and reported on the software page with its design, its confidence intervals and its stated limits.
good.realWorld: The problem is anchored in The Lancet's 2024 global burden estimate: 4.71 million deaths associated with bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2021, 1.14 million attributable to it, and a reference-scenario projection of roughly 1.91 million attributable deaths annually by 2050, with knock-on effects on surgery and cancer care that depend on effective infection control. The named audiences are AMP researchers at universities and research institutions, synthetic biology and iGEM teams, and early-stage R&D professionals in biopharmaceutical companies. The team frames the longer-term goal as making the workflow reusable for other functional peptides by swapping domain knowledge, generation and evaluation models and experimental requirements. Contributions are offered at three independently usable levels: the software and its interfaces, an organised AMP knowledge base, and human practices questions and editable records for connecting stakeholder engagement to design.
partners: Dr Justin Fendos (Yale Teaching Center / Dongseo Scientific Teaching Center)

gemsTakeaway: Make the application, not the model, own the research record: AMPilot checks a stage complete against saved outputs rather than a conversational claim, reconciles promised work against what was actually written because a fluent closing message is not a delivery receipt, and shortens repeated context by replacing bodies with indexes that name exactly how to read the detail again instead of substituting an AI summary. Then prove the tool's value the way they did, with a randomised AB/BA crossover study reporting completion, time with confidence intervals, error counts and SUS, and with a published list of exactly which CI tests were skipped and why.
